source_text: Quod autem Deus dictus est: Figulus ex eadem massa faciens aliud vas in honorem, aliud in contumeliam [n326] , a te commemorari omnino non debuit; quia ut a nobis consequenter exponitur, ita tibi totum repugnat; nam cum alii in honorem, alii in contumeliam fieri dicuntur, iuvatur sensus Catholicorum, quo secundum diversitatem voluntatis humanae, diversus etiam vasorum exitus praedicatur.
pass_a_gloss: But that God has been said: A potter from the same mass making another vessel unto honor, another unto insult, ought not at all to have been recalled by you; because as it is consequently expounded by us, so the whole fights you; for when some are said to be made unto honor, others unto insult, the sense of the Catholics is helped, by which according to the diversity of human will, a diverse exit also of the vessels is preached.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: You should never have mentioned that God is called “the potter making from the same lump one vessel for honor and another for dishonor” (Romans 9:21). For as we explain it consistently, it wholly opposes you. When some are said to be made for honor and others for dishonor, this supports the catholic understanding that the different outcomes of the vessels correspond to the differences in human will.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
